label: Claude Sonnet 5.5
output:
Hi Bergeron, and hi everyone,

Thank you for asking me directly. You're right that people deserve a straight answer before the 4th, and I'm sorry it took a thread on the board for me to give it. I wanted to keep a surprise for the reopening, but I can't let people worry for a week, so here it is.

**We are not closing and we are not moving. We bought the building.**

Marc-Antoine's cousin is half right: the building was sold in the fall. It was sold to me. M. Ferland, who owned it, is 81 and is retiring to Sherbrooke to be with his daughter. He offered to sell to me before anybody else, and we signed at the notary on December 15. I won't tell you everything about that day, but M. Ferland has come in every morning for 17 years for his baguette pas trop cuite, and he cried a little at the notary. So did I, a little. No condos, no bank, no vape shop. Just the bakery, for a good while longer.

**So what is the closing for?** Works. We're closed from January 4 to 18 and we reopen **Tuesday, January 19, at 7h**, same as always. Here is what's happening during those two weeks:

- A new deck oven, 4 decks, coming from a supplier in Laval. The old one is from 1998 and broke down three times this year. I was tired of praying every morning before turning it on, and I think the bread will be better for it too.
- We're taking the space at the back, the old storage of the dépanneur. We'll put in 6 small tables, so for the first time you can sit down with your coffee and your croissant instead of eating on the sidewalk in January.

**About the sign.** My nephew Thomas wrote it at 6 in the morning, and "Grande nouvelle bientôt" was his idea. I said ok without thinking, and I clearly should have thought. I can see now how it looks from the street, and I'm sorry for the stress. Thomas has been told.

**About the shelves** looking half empty on the 28th: that was only Christmas. We sold everything for Christmas Eve, including 400 bûches, and I'm still recovering. It had nothing to do with closing.

**Now the carnets, because this is the part that matters most.** We sold 214 of them in October, $60 for 12 loaves. They are all still good, and they have no expiry date. Whatever you have left on yours, whether it's 7 loaves or 11, it's honoured when we reopen. As a thank you for your patience, every carnet holder also gets one free croissant in January.

And if anybody is worried and wants their money back, just come and see me, before the 4th or after we reopen on the 19th. I give it back, no question, no explanation needed. I'd be sad to see you go, but I'd rather you trust me or have your money than be stressed about it.

I'll be honest about one thing. I understand why people worry. Mile End has lost a lot of small shops, and everyone has seen a "closed, big news soon" sign turn into something sad. So I'm not angry that people asked. But when I read the word "scam," it hurt. I've been on this street since March 2009, I know many of you by name, and I know whose kid takes the chocolatine and whose husband likes the crust very dark. I would not do that to this street. Of course, I also know that a sign like that made it easy to think it, so I take my share.

**To the people living upstairs:** I know you were probably the most worried of all. The 3 apartments stay rented, with the same tenants and the same rent. I promised each of you in writing, and I mean it. Nobody is going anywhere. Please come and see me if you have any questions at all.

**Thank you** to Priya, and to everyone else who spoke up for us on this thread, and who didn't wait for the answer to give us the benefit of the doubt. Priya, the chocolatines were my pleasure, and your kid can have another one on the 19th. It means a lot to me to read that after 17 years on this street, and more than I can write here. Thank you also to the people who asked hard questions, because it's what made me finally write all this down.

**And please come celebrate with us.** On **Saturday, January 23**, we're having a reopening party. Everyone is invited, carnet or no carnet, neighbours, curious people, even those who were sure we were closing. There will be coffee on us and a free piece of the first new bread from the new oven. Come see the little tables at the back, and sit down, finally.

To summarize for the ones who only read the last paragraph:

- Closed January 4 to 18 for works
- Reopening Tuesday, January 19, at 7h
- Party on Saturday, January 23, coffee and new bread free for everyone
- Carnets stay valid, with a free croissant in January, or your money back on request
- Upstairs tenants: same people, same rent
- Not closing, not moving. We own the building now.

Thank you for caring about the bakery. It makes me very happy to know you do.

Hélène
Boulangerie Le Pétrin Doré, Fairmount

---

I didn't give a time for the party on the 23rd since you didn't mention one. If you have hours in mind, add them in the invitation paragraph. Also, check that you're happy with the line about the croissant for carnet holders being valid on the days you're open in January, since the shop is closed for the first half of the month.
